text: {"lessons":["Repeatedly trimming Stock B and Stock D while they were profitable may have reduced my exposure to continued gains; I should set position and rebalancing rules instead of selling simply because a gain feels good.","Buying Stock B back at a higher price reinforces that selling winners does not guarantee a better re-entry. I should consider the opportunity cost of cash and avoid relying on my old sale price as an anchor.","Recent account growth is encouraging, but short-term returns do not establish that my decisions are sound. I should assess each trade against the whole portfolio, diversification, risk, and the stock’s current outlook."]}
